object_types.name: Account
object_types.definition: A company or organization that has signed up for subscriptions to products. Identified by a six-digit sequential account number that is never reused.

source_references.excerpt: Every account has an account number. That's what everything hangs off... Six digits, sequential, never reused.
Unpack "customer" first. What is a customer in the system? An account.

object_types.name: AccountNumber
object_types.definition: A unique six-digit sequential identifier assigned to an account, never reused.

source_references.excerpt: Every account has an account number... Six digits, sequential, never reused.

object_types.name: Subscription
object_types.definition: An agreement that an account pays for access to a product at a specified price on a billing cycle. Identified by a subscription ID prefixed with SUB.

source_references.excerpt: A subscription is the agreement that this account pays us this amount on this cycle for this thing. It's got a subscription ID... Unique. Generated, prefixed with SUB.

object_types.name: SubscriptionID
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a subscription, generated and prefixed with SUB.

source_references.excerpt: It's got a subscription ID... Unique. Generated, prefixed with SUB.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: A service offering that customers can subscribe to. Currently three products exist: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.

source_references.excerpt: Product code. We have three: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.
Product code. We have three: CORE, ANALYTICS, and CONNECT.

object_types.name: PricePlan
object_types.definition: A billing artifact that specifies what a customer pays and how often (monthly or annually). Examples: CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490. Each price plan entitles exactly one feature bundle.

source_references.excerpt: The price plan. It's got a plan code, it says what the customer pays and how often. CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.
And I mean the billing artefact. The thing that generates the invoice line.

object_types.name: PlanCode
object_types.definition: A code identifying a price plan.

source_references.excerpt: It's got a plan code, it says what the customer pays and how often.

object_types.name: FeatureBundle
object_types.definition: A feature set offered to customers, defining seats, API access, SSO, and other capabilities. Examples: Starter, Professional, Enterprise. Identified by its name.

source_references.excerpt: When I say plan I mean what the customer gets. Starter, Professional, Enterprise. It's the feature bundle -- how many seats, whether they get the API, whether they get SSO.
Name. Starter, Professional, Enterprise... Is the name unique? Yes. There's exactly one Professional.

object_types.name: BundleName
object_types.definition: The name of a feature bundle (Starter, Professional, or Enterprise).

source_references.excerpt: Name. Starter, Professional, Enterprise. There's exactly one Professional.

object_types.name: StartDate
object_types.definition: The date on which a subscription begins. Mandatory for every subscription.

source_references.excerpt: Start date. End date, sometimes... Start date is always there. You can't create a subscription without one, the form won't submit.

object_types.name: EndDate
object_types.definition: The date on which a subscription ends. Optional; open-ended subscriptions have no end date.

source_references.excerpt: Start date. End date, sometimes... An open-ended subscription has no end date. Most of them are open-ended -- they run until cancelled.

object_types.name: BillingPeriod
object_types.definition: The frequency at which a customer is billed. Either monthly or annual, never both for a single subscription.

source_references.excerpt: Billing period -- what are the values? Monthly or annual... Every subscription has exactly one billing period.

object_types.name: SubscriptionStatus
object_types.definition: The current state of a subscription. One of: trialing, active, past due, cancelled. Every subscription is in exactly one status.

source_references.excerpt: Status? Trialing, active, past due, cancelled... Exactly one, yes.

object_types.name: PlanChange
object_types.definition: A record of a change to a subscription's price plan. Identifies the new plan, effective date, and who requested it. Allows tracking the historical plan for revenue purposes.

source_references.excerpt: A change is a record. We don't overwrite the plan on the subscription, we write a plan change with an effective date... It has to, because we need to know who made it and when it takes effect, and those are different dates.

object_types.name: ChangeID
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a plan change.

source_references.excerpt: So a plan change is its own thing, with its own identity? It's got a change ID.

object_types.name: EffectiveDate
object_types.definition: The date on which a plan change takes effect, which may differ from the date the change was requested.

source_references.excerpt: we write a plan change with an effective date... Someone can make a change on the third that takes effect on the first of next month.

object_types.name: Requester
object_types.definition: The identifier of the person who requested a plan change.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between Account and Subscription cardinality in the 'is for' relationship. While 'one active subscription per account per product' is stated, it is unclear whether an inactive/cancelled subscription still belongs to the same account or whether terminated subscriptions are retained in the model. The uniqueness constraint is stated as 'one active subscription per account per product', but it's not explicit whether there can be multiple non-active subscriptions per account per product (e.g., multiple cancelled subscriptions).

source_references.excerpt: An account has one active subscription... one active subscription per account per product, enforced at the database level.

ambiguities.description: The 'paused' status on subscriptions. The transcript indicates that 'paused' is a separate boolean flag that overlaps with the status field, causing bugs in queries. It is unclear whether 'paused' should be modeled as part of the subscription status value type or remain as a separate attribute not included in the ORM model. This creates a potential constraint interaction that is not fully resolved.

source_references.excerpt: There's also paused... Paused isn't a status, it's a flag... If you ask the system for active subscriptions you get paused ones too.

ambiguities.description: Mid-term cancellation on annual subscriptions and refunds. The transcript explicitly identifies this as an unresolved business rule: whether a customer who cancels an annual subscription mid-term should receive a prorated refund, a credit, or no refund. The system currently sets an end date and allows access to run, but the commercial policy is undecided. This creates ambiguity about whether a refund/credit concept should be modeled.

source_references.excerpt: Someone signs an annual deal in January, pays up front, cancels in April. What happens?... The model will capture the system behaviour, which is that cancellation sets an end date and access runs to it, and it will not invent a refund concept that doesn't exist.

ambiguities.description: Whether a subscription can have zero plan changes or if a newly created subscription must have an implicit initial plan change. The transcript states that 'a brand new subscription has none' (plan changes), implying that the Subscription uses PricePlan fact is the current plan field, but it's unclear whether this should be modeled as derived from the most recent plan change or as an independent stored field.

source_references.excerpt: And a brand new subscription has none... the subscription does carry a current price plan, and the change records are the history behind it.

ambiguities.description: Contact information is mentioned as separate from Account. Priya states 'Email is on the contact, not the account,' but no Contact entity type or relationship to Account is modeled. It is unclear whether contact management is in scope for this data model or if it should be explicitly excluded.

source_references.excerpt: Is there anything else that identifies an account? Email, company name? Company name absolutely not, we have four accounts called 'Acme.' Email is on the contact, not the account.

ambiguities.description: Whether a Product can be without any PricePlan offerings. The transcript states that a bundle can exist without a price plan ('we build a bundle before we price it'), but it is not explicitly stated whether a Product must have at least one active PricePlan. Similarly, the lifecycle of price plans (when they are retired or deprecated) is not discussed.

source_references.excerpt: And can a bundle exist with no price plan pointing at it? Yes -- we build a bundle before we price it. Enterprise existed for two months before there was anything to buy.

ambiguities.description: The cost/amount values on a PricePlan. The transcript references 'what the customer pays' (e.g., CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490), implying a price, but no Price or Amount value type is modeled because the facilitator defers this to the price plan itself. It is unclear whether a PricePlan should include explicit Price and Currency attributes, or if these are implicitly encoded in the plan code.

source_references.excerpt: The price plan. It's got a plan code, it says what the customer pays and how often. CORE-MO-49, CORE-AN-490, that kind of thing.

ambiguities.description: The exact meaning and scope of 'active' subscription status. The transcript uses both 'active status' and 'one active subscription per account per product,' but it is unclear whether the status value 'active' is synonymous with 'current/ongoing' or if there are subscriptions with 'active' status that are not 'active' in the business sense (e.g., past due).

source_references.excerpt: An account has one active subscription... Status? Trialing, active, past due, cancelled.

ambiguities.description: Whether the current plan field on Subscription is derived from the plan change history or independently stored and maintained. The transcript initially suggests it is derived ('The subscription's current plan is derived from the change history') but later indicates it is a denormalized field that is 'maintained by the change process.' It is unclear how conflicts are resolved if the stored current plan and the derived plan from change history disagree, other than 'the change history wins and the current plan is the bug.'

source_references.excerpt: the subscription's current plan is derived from the change history... it does have a current plan field... If those two ever disagree, the change history wins and the current plan is the bug.
